explanations: record() holds a pooled connection for its whole transaction and then calls audit.record(), which checks out a second connection from the same pool. When as many results are recorded at once as the pool has connections, every request holds one connection and waits for another that will never be released. That is a resource deadlock from nested acquisition, with no error or timeout, only a stall. Writing the audit entry on the connection already held (audit.write(conn, ...)) means each request needs one connection, so the pool can't be exhausted this way. It also puts the audit entry inside the same transaction, so it rolls back with the result instead of being committed on its own.
